followup_reviews.Research finding: Retain the Serbian freight protest as an included parent with two distinct operational phases, rather than one national uniform closure interval. The first phase concerns participating cargo terminals and excludes passengers; the second concerns the later Serbian-side Montenegro freight action in both directions. Individual exemptions/terminal implementation remain qualified. Retain 26–30 January 2026, four calendar days, for the regional Serbian action and 29–30 January, one calendar day, for the Montenegro-frontier extension. The latter is reported as less than 24 hours; no full-day or precise elapsed-hour assertion is introduced. Schengen driver stay/admission rules and transport protest demands support Migration / Admission and document disputes and Trade / Trade and transport protests. Montenegro’s domestic fuel/VAT demands are not automatically assigned to Serbian protesters. Reuters onset and ANSA ending accounts were directly read. The Vijesti English page is explicitly AI translated, so its clock wording is qualified. KoSSev’s failed retrieval provides no new confirmation. Both phases remain unlocated, preventing a country-level report from colouring every terminal with identical dates. No maritime facility is added.
